raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57159. Thanks to @nilig for the report and producer/consumer analysis.

An offloaded complete chunk is retrieved by its final block hash, but its
self-describing event currently advertises the constituent GPU-block hashes
as separate cache units. A request sharing only an interior prefix can
therefore appear to hit the CPU cache even though lookup misses.

This change advertises each complete chunk with its final hash and complete
token count as `block_size`. `BlockRemoved` uses the same saved chunk hash.
The preceding chunk's hash remains the parent. Existing tests and the option
documentation are updated to the corrected representation.

### Scope and compatibility

- Only self-describing complete-chunk event metadata changes. Cache keys,
  allocation, lookup, transfers, eviction, and generation are unchanged.
- Single-block chunks, opt-out/placeholder behavior, and partial recurrent
  tails retain their existing representation.
- No wire-schema field or default changes. Consumers must nevertheless honor
  the complete retrieval unit instead of splitting it into partial hits.
- The separate consumer issue llm-d/llm-d-router#2889 is not fixed here.

### Duplicate-work check

On 2026-09-17, the issue had no assignee or claim comments. PR searches for
`57159`, `offloading events`, and retrieval/chunk granularity found no direct
implementation. Related #52103 changes event provenance and metadata
lifetime, but the inspected patch retains per-GPU-block granularity. This
patch is limited to retrieval granularity; happy to coordinate merge order
and the event contract with that work.

## Test Plan

The new CPU-level regression pairs the actual `CPUOffloadingManager` with
`OffloadingEventsTracker`: a stored 64-token chunk is queried with shared
prefixes of 0, 16, 32, 48, and 64 tokens, using hash sizes of 4 and 16 tokens.
Additional cases check that overlapping chunks store/remove distinct hashes.
Existing tests retain coverage for parents, groups, promotion, placeholders,
and partial tails. GPU worker tests cover actual CPU/GPU transfers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q

VLLM_KV_EVENTS_USE_INT_BLOCK_HASHES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

## Test Result

Validated against main `2d8a5c5741dedb3559d26ce95fa894771cffa881`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original existing event suite | 23 passed |
| Initial reproduction on original implementation | 6 expected failures, 4 passing controls |
| Patched event suite (includes 13 new cases) | 36 passed |
| Patched event suite with byte hashes | 36 passed |
| Connector/scheduler/CPU manager/tiering regression | 580 passed, 1 collection skip |
| GPU worker regression | 39 passed, 1 skip |
| All 13 new cases with original production file restored | 9 expected failures, 4 passing controls |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` | Passed |

The focused tests are included in the 580 count, not additional unique tests.
The two skips are missing optional `kvcr` and a ROCm-only case on NVIDIA.

Environment: RTX PRO 5000 72 GB Blackwell, Python 3.10.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu130.
Current-main Python source was installed editably using existing vLLM 0.27.1
precompiled native artifacts; this was not a fresh native build. Source paths
and all tracked regular-file hashes were verified. Tests ran offline.

Model evaluation: not run. This patch changes event metadata rather than
model computation or cache contents; no generation-quality, throughput, or
end-to-end router correctness result is claimed. Upstream CI has not run yet.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used for investigation, implementation,
regression tests, and test execution. The original issue supplied the
retrieval-boundary diagnosis.

nodes.body:
This does not work with Dynamo.

Dynamo uses one global block size for its KV index. GPU events still use the GPU block size, such as 16, while this PR makes CPU events use the chunk size, such as 64. Dynamo will reject all CPU events.

We need to keep one block size and represent CPU chunk separately.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @wuhangxian.
